text: A tiger's roar can be heard from about three kilometres away.
Pugs were bred in ancient China, well over a thousand years ago, as companions for royal families.
Axolotls, a kind of salamander, can regrow whole legs, and even parts of their heart and brain.
Super Mario first appeared in 1981 in a game called Donkey Kong, where he was called Jumpman.
The modern circus began in London in 1768, with a horse rider called Philip Astley.
Farfalle means butterflies, orecchiette means little ears, and linguine means little tongues.
Potatoes were the first vegetable grown in space, in 1995 on the space shuttle Columbia.
A teaspoon of a neutron star would weigh about a billion tonnes.
Light is so fast that it could go around the Earth about seven and a half times in one second.
Your heart beats about 100,000 times every day.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
Antarctica is a desert. It is the driest, windiest and coldest continent on Earth.
The word "dinosaur" means "terrible lizard", and it was invented in 1842 by a scientist called Richard Owen.
The Wright brothers' first powered flight, in 1903, lasted 12 seconds and covered about 37 metres.
The Pacific Ocean is bigger than all of the land on Earth put together.
A pangram is a sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet, like "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog".
A piano has 88 keys.
A marathon is 42.195 kilometres because of the 1908 Olympics in London, when the route was measured from Windsor Castle to the stadium.
Thunder is the sound of the air around a bolt of lightning heating up and expanding suddenly.
Most of the ocean floor has never been explored in detail. We have better maps of the surface of Mars than of the sea floor.
Some types of bamboo can grow nearly a metre in a single day.
An ant can carry something 10 to 50 times heavier than itself.
The idea of zero as a number was worked out in India about 1,400 years ago.
The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world, at more than 800 metres.
The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci more than 500 years ago, and hangs in the Louvre museum in Paris.
Water is unusual because it gets bigger when it freezes, which is why ice floats.
The seven-day week comes from ancient Babylon.
Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first people to reach the top of Mount Everest, in 1953.
A wandering albatross has a wingspan of up to about three and a half metres, and can glide for hours without flapping.
A chameleon can shoot out its tongue almost twice as far as the length of its own body.
Elephants can send low rumbles through the ground that other elephants can feel through their feet from far away.
You have about 100,000 hairs on your head.
A tiger's tongue is covered in tiny hooked spikes. They scrape meat off bones, and work like a comb when it washes.
A famous story says a pug named Pompey saved a Dutch prince in 1572 by barking when soldiers crept up on his tent.
Tardigrades, or water bears, are tiny animals that survived being taken into outer space with no protection.
The first home video game console, the Magnavox Odyssey, came out in 1972. It had no sound at all.
The word "circus" is Latin for "ring" or "circle".
Al dente means "to the tooth". It describes pasta cooked so it is still a little firm to bite.
Ramen noodles are yellow and springy because of a mineral salt added to the dough, called kansui.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the biggest volcano we know of, about two and a half times as tall as Mount Everest.
Sound travels more than four times faster in water than in air.
Babies are born with no kneecaps, only soft cartilage that hardens into bone as they grow.
The Great Pyramid was the tallest human-made structure in the world for nearly 4,000 years.
The Sahara was once green, with lakes and grassland, until around 5,000 years ago.
Tyrannosaurus rex had teeth as long as bananas, if you count the part hidden in the jaw.
The first email was sent in 1971 by Ray Tomlinson, who chose the @ sign to separate the name from the computer.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level, but Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller from its base, which is deep under the ocean.
The word "robot" comes from a Czech play written in 1920. It comes from "robota", which means hard work.
Mozart wrote his first pieces of music when he was only five years old.
The Olympic Games began in ancient Greece, traditionally in 776 BC.
Raindrops are not shaped like teardrops. Small ones are round, and big ones are squashed like burger buns.
Sunlight fades out about 200 metres down in the ocean, and below about 1,000 metres it is completely dark.
Young sunflowers turn their faces to follow the Sun across the sky.
A dragonfly can fly in any direction, including backwards and sideways.
Pi is the number you get when you divide the distance round a circle by the distance across it. It starts 3.14159 and never ends.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa started to lean while it was being built, because the ground on one side was soft.
Leonardo da Vinci wrote his notebooks in mirror writing, so you need a mirror to read them easily.
Gold is so soft that it can be hammered into sheets so thin you can see light through them.
Wednesday is named after the Norse god Woden, also called Odin, and Thursday after Thor.
Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon, in 1969.
A peregrine falcon can dive at more than 300 kilometres an hour, which makes it the fastest animal on Earth.
Frogs can breathe through their skin.
Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly.
Your fingerprints are formed before you are born, and they never change as you grow.
White tigers are not a separate kind of tiger. A rare change in one gene stops them making their orange colour.
A dog's nose print is unique, just like a human fingerprint.
The mimic octopus can copy other sea creatures, like lionfish and sea snakes, to scare off enemies.
Pong was Atari's first game. Its creator, Allan Alcorn, was given it as a simple practice project.
Circus rings are almost always about 13 metres wide, the size that lets a horse gallop round while its rider stands on its back.
Spaghetti is a plural word. One single strand is a spaghetto.
It takes about ten litres of milk to make one kilogram of hard cheese.
A day on Mars is about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
Count the seconds between a flash of lightning and the thunder, then divide by three, to get how far away it is in kilometres.
The hardest substance in your body is tooth enamel.
The University of Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire: teaching there began over 900 years ago.
Papua New Guinea has about 840 languages, more than any other country.
Birds are living dinosaurs. They are descended from small feathered dinosaurs.
Alexander Graham Bell's first telephone call, in 1876, is said to have been "Mr Watson, come here".
The Amazon carries more water than any other river on Earth.
"Hippopotamus" means "river horse" in Greek.
Beethoven kept writing music even after he went deaf.
Tennis balls were mostly white until the 1970s, when yellow ones became popular because they were easier to see on television.
Snowflakes have six sides, because of the way water molecules join together as ice.
Many deep-sea animals make their own light, which is called bioluminescence.
Some bristlecone pine trees in California are nearly 5,000 years old, which makes them among the oldest living things on Earth.
Fireflies make light with a chemical reaction that gives off almost no heat.
A googol is a 1 followed by 100 zeros. The company Google took its name from it, with a spelling mistake.
The dome of the Pantheon in Rome, built about 1,900 years ago, is still the biggest dome in the world made from concrete with no metal inside.
Aesop's fables, including The Tortoise and the Hare, were first told about 2,500 years ago.
Glass is made mostly from sand, melted at a very high temperature.
July and August are named after the Roman rulers Julius Caesar and Augustus.
Yuri Gagarin was the first person in space, in 1961. His trip lasted 108 minutes.
Flamingos are pink because of the colourful chemicals in the food they eat.
A poison dart frog's bright colours are a warning to hungry animals.
Koalas have fingerprints almost the same as human fingerprints.
Your tongue print is as unique as your fingerprint.
The backs of a tiger's ears have white spots that look like eyes. Some scientists think they help tigers signal to each other, or make other animals feel watched.
Dogs can smell thousands of times better than people. Some are trained to sniff out lost people, and even certain illnesses.
A pistol shrimp snaps its claw so fast that a bubble forms and bursts with a bang loud enough to stun small fish.
The designer of Pac-Man said the shape came from a pizza with a slice missing.
The trapeze act was made famous in the 1850s by a Frenchman, Jules Léotard. The leotard is named after him.
Pesto comes from the Italian city of Genoa. Its name comes from a word meaning to pound, because it was made in a mortar.
Popcorn pops because a tiny drop of water inside each kernel turns to steam and bursts the shell.
Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is the furthest human-made object from Earth, over 20 billion kilometres away. A radio message takes about a day to reach it.
Your brain uses about a fifth of all the energy your body makes, even though it is only about two per cent of your weight.
The smallest bone in your body is in your ear. It is smaller than a grain of rice.
The Terracotta Army in China has about 8,000 clay soldiers, and no two faces seem to be the same.
Nepal's flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle.
Some dinosaurs had feathers, including some relatives of Tyrannosaurus rex.
Penicillin was discovered in 1928 by Alexander Fleming, when mould grew on one of his dishes and killed the bacteria around it.
Greenland is the biggest island in the world. Australia is counted as a continent, not an island.
"Orangutan" means "person of the forest" in Malay.
The didgeridoo, played by Aboriginal Australians, is one of the oldest wind instruments in the world.
Basketball was invented in 1891 by a teacher, James Naismith. The first baskets were peach baskets.
Hailstones can grow as big as grapefruits. The biggest ever found in the United States was about 20 centimetres across.
Anglerfish have a glowing lure that dangles in front of their mouths to attract prey in the dark.
The tallest trees, coast redwoods, can grow taller than 110 metres, higher than a 30-storey building.
Insects have six legs and spiders have eight, so spiders are not insects.
A prime number can only be divided by 1 and itself. Two is the only even prime number.
The Colosseum in Rome could hold about 50,000 people.
Shakespeare is credited with first using many everyday words, including "eyeball" and "bedroom".
Rust is what happens when iron joins up with oxygen and water.
September comes from the Latin word for seven, because it was once the seventh month of the year.
Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space, in 1963.
An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain.
The Komodo dragon is the biggest lizard in the world, and can grow to about three metres long.
A hippo's skin makes a red-orange liquid that works like sunscreen and helps keep germs away.
Your liver can regrow itself after being damaged, which is very unusual for an organ.
Three kinds of tiger have died out in about the last hundred years: the Bali, Javan and Caspian tigers.
A border collie named Chaser learned the names of more than 1,000 different toys.
Bar-headed geese fly over the Himalayas, higher than 7,000 metres, where there is far less oxygen than at ground level.
The Minecraft creeper was an accident: its creator said he mixed up the height and width numbers while making a pig.
In 1859, Charles Blondin crossed Niagara Falls on a tightrope, and later did it blindfolded, on stilts, and carrying a man on his back.
Pasta was eaten in Italy long before tomatoes arrived there from the Americas in the 1500s.
Orange carrots were made popular by Dutch growers in the 1600s. Before that, many carrots were purple or yellow.
The Sun holds 99.8 per cent of all the mass in our solar system.
If you could stretch out the DNA from one of your cells, it would be about two metres long.
Red blood cells live for about four months, and your body makes about two million new ones every second.
Big Ben is not the clock or the tower. It is the nickname of the huge bell inside.
Russia has 11 time zones.
Argentinosaurus was one of the biggest dinosaurs: about as long as three buses parked end to end.
Louis Braille was blind from the age of three, and invented his system of raised dots for reading when he was only 15.
Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake in the world, and holds about a fifth of all the fresh water in the world's lakes.
"Mosquito" means "little fly" in Spanish.
Talking drums in West Africa can copy the rise and fall of speech so well that messages can be sent over long distances.
Golf balls have dimples because they make the ball fly further.
The seasons happen because the Earth is tilted, not because it gets closer to or further from the Sun.
The giant squid has the biggest eyes of any animal, as big as a dinner plate.
A Venus flytrap only snaps shut if something touches its hairs twice within about 20 seconds, so it does not waste energy on raindrops.
Inside its chrysalis, a caterpillar almost completely dissolves and rebuilds itself as a butterfly.
The angles inside any triangle always add up to 180 degrees.
The London Underground opened in 1863 and was the first underground railway in the world.
Origami is Japanese for "folding paper".
Breathing in helium makes your voice squeaky because sound travels faster through helium than through air.
A fortnight is short for "fourteen nights".
Amelia Earhart was the first woman to fly alone across the Atlantic, in 1932.
Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards.
Crocodiles cannot stick their tongues out.
Cats can rotate their ears almost all the way round to pinpoint a sound.
Hiccups happen when the muscle under your lungs, the diaphragm, suddenly twitches.
The Amur tiger, the biggest kind, can weigh more than 200 kilograms and lives in forests that get as cold as minus 30 degrees.
Greyhounds can run at about 70 kilometres an hour, as fast as a car driving through a town.
An Arctic tern flies from the Arctic to Antarctica and back every year, a journey of more than 70,000 kilometres.
Pokémon was inspired by its creator Satoshi Tajiri's childhood hobby of collecting insects.
Cirque du Soleil began in 1984 in Quebec, with a group of street performers.
A real wheel of Parmesan weighs about 40 kilograms and takes at least a year to age.
Chillies feel hot because of a chemical called capsaicin. Birds cannot feel it, so they spread the seeds.
Venus is the hottest planet, at about 465 degrees Celsius, even hotter than Mercury, because its thick clouds trap heat.
The sky is blue because air scatters the blue part of sunlight much more than the red part.
Your brain cannot feel pain, even though it tells you about everything else that hurts.
The shortest war in history, in 1896, lasted less than an hour.
The Dead Sea is so salty that you float on top of it without trying.
Velociraptor was about the size of a turkey, and it had feathers. The ones in films are much bigger than the real animal.
The first computer mouse, made in the 1960s, had a wooden case.
Africa has 54 countries, more than any other continent.
The word "alphabet" comes from the first two letters of the Greek alphabet: alpha and beta.
Most orchestras tune to a note played by the oboe.
The 100 metres world record is 9.58 seconds, set by Usain Bolt in 2009.
At the equator, the Earth's surface is spinning at about 1,600 kilometres an hour.
The sea is salty because rivers wash tiny amounts of salt out of rocks and carry it down to the ocean.
A strawberry wears its seeds on the outside.
Monarch butterflies migrate up to 4,000 kilometres to spend the winter somewhere warm.
The Fibonacci numbers, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, and so on, appear in the spirals of sunflower seeds and pine cones.
The Channel Tunnel is about 50 kilometres long, and a train takes about 35 minutes to go through it.
Toy Story, in 1995, was the first full-length film made entirely with computer animation.
Baking soda and vinegar fizz when they are mixed, because they make a gas called carbon dioxide.
Atomic clocks are so accurate that they would take millions of years to be wrong by even a second.
Roald Amundsen and his team were the first to reach the South Pole, in 1911.
A woodpecker's tongue is so long that it wraps around the back of its skull.
A tortoise's shell is part of its skeleton, joined to its backbone and ribs.
A giraffe's tongue is about 45 centimetres long, and it is dark purple, probably to protect it from sunburn.
Goosebumps are left over from when our ancestors were much hairier, and puffed up their fur to stay warm.
A tiger can see in the dark roughly six times better than you, thanks to a mirror-like layer at the back of its eyes.
Dalmatian puppies are born pure white. Their spots appear when they are a few weeks old.
A hummingbird's heart can beat more than 1,000 times a minute.
In 1979, a game called Adventure hid the first known "Easter egg": its programmer secretly put his name in a hidden room.
The first human cannonball act in Britain was in 1877, by a teenage performer called Zazel.
A honeybee makes only about a twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole life.
Saturn's moon Titan has rivers and lakes, but they are full of liquid methane, not water.
The Earth's core is about as hot as the surface of the Sun.
Fingernails grow faster than toenails, by about three millimetres a month.
The Vikings sailed to North America around the year 1000, about 500 years before Columbus.
Tokyo is the biggest city in the world, with around 37 million people living in and around it.
Fossils form when minerals slowly replace the bones of a dead animal, turning them to stone.
The first bicycle, built in 1817, had no pedals. Riders pushed it along with their feet.
The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is about 11 kilometres deep. If you dropped Mount Everest into it, the top would still be more than two kilometres under water.
"Quarantine" comes from an Italian phrase meaning "forty days".
Violins made by Antonio Stradivari in Italy more than 300 years ago are still played, and are worth millions.
Skateboarding became an Olympic sport at the Tokyo Games.
Mauna Loa in Hawaii is the biggest active volcano on Earth.
Male seahorses carry the eggs in a pouch and give birth to the babies.
Chocolate is made from the seeds of a tropical tree called cacao.
Termite mounds can be several metres tall, with tunnels that work like air conditioning.
A Rubik's Cube can be arranged in more than 43 quintillion different ways. That is 43 followed by 18 zeros.
The colour of the Golden Gate Bridge is called "International Orange".
Dr Seuss wrote "Green Eggs and Ham" using only 50 different words, after a bet with his publisher.
Soap works because one end of its molecules grabs water and the other end grabs grease.
The ancient Egyptians used sundials and water clocks to tell the time about 3,500 years ago.
Marie Curie is the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, physics and chemistry.
Common swifts can stay in the air for ten months without landing, even sleeping while they fly.
Snakes smell with their tongues, which is why they flick them in and out.
A rhino's horn is made from keratin, the same material as your hair and fingernails.
You cannot tickle yourself, because your brain predicts the touch before it happens.
Unlike most cats, tigers love water. They are strong swimmers and can swim for several kilometres.
A pug's flat face makes it harder for it to cool down, which is why pugs get hot so quickly. Dogs cool down mostly by panting.
Crows can recognise human faces, and remember who was kind or unkind to them for years.
In Super Mario Bros, the clouds and the bushes are the same drawing in different colours.
Tightrope walkers hold long poles because they make them steadier: the pole lowers their balance point.
A year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years.
Diamond and the lead in a pencil are both made of carbon, just arranged in different ways.
Your skin is your body's biggest organ. An adult's covers about two square metres.
Machu Picchu, in Peru, was built by the Inca more than 500 years ago, high in the mountains.
The Eiffel Tower can grow about 15 centimetres taller in hot weather, because metal expands when it warms up.
Mary Anning began finding fossils as a child in the early 1800s and became one of the most important fossil hunters ever.
The first sliced bread was sold in 1928 in the American state of Missouri.
Angel Falls in Venezuela is the tallest waterfall in the world, at nearly a kilometre high.
The word "muscle" comes from a Latin word meaning "little mouse", because some muscles look like mice moving under the skin.
The theremin is an instrument you play without touching it, by moving your hands near two metal antennas.
Trampolining became an Olympic sport at the 2000 Sydney Games.
The ground beneath us is made of giant plates that move very slowly, about as fast as your fingernails grow.
Coral reefs cover less than one per cent of the sea floor, yet about a quarter of all sea creatures live in or near them.
Vanilla comes from the pod of an orchid.
A ladybird's bright spots are a warning to hungry birds that it tastes horrible.
The Rubik's Cube was invented in 1974 by a Hungarian professor, Ernő Rubik, to help teach his students about 3D shapes.
The Taj Mahal in India was built about 400 years ago as a tomb, and took more than 20 years to finish.
Beatrix Potter first told the story of Peter Rabbit in a letter to a sick child.
Hot air balloons rise because hot air is lighter than the cooler air around it.
A leap year has 366 days, with an extra day on 29 February.
Ada Lovelace, who lived in the 1800s, is often called the first computer programmer.
A puffin can carry a dozen small fish in its beak at one time.
Geckos can walk up walls and across ceilings thanks to millions of microscopic hairs on their feet.
Pangolins are the only mammals covered in scales, and they curl into a ball when they are scared.
Your small intestine is about six metres long, coiled up inside you, about as long as a minibus.
A male lion and a female tiger can have a cub called a liger, which can grow bigger than either parent.
Dogs have a third eyelid, a thin one that sweeps sideways across the eye to keep it clean.
Dolphins give each other names: each one has its own whistle, and its friends call it back.
Sonic the Hedgehog was created in 1991 as a mascot for Sega, to take on Mario.
People have been juggling for thousands of years: there is an ancient Egyptian painting of jugglers that is about 4,000 years old.
The International Space Station circles the Earth about every 90 minutes, so astronauts see around 16 sunrises a day.
About half of the oxygen we breathe comes from tiny ocean plants called phytoplankton.
You blink about 15 to 20 times every minute.
The oldest known cave paintings, found in Indonesia, are more than 45,000 years old.
Triceratops means "three-horned face".
The three-point seat belt was invented in 1959 by an engineer called Nils Bohlin, who gave the idea away for free to save lives.
The word "geyser" comes from Geysir, a famous hot spring in Iceland.
"Pyjamas" is a word borrowed from Urdu and Hindi, and "ketchup" probably comes from a Chinese word for fish sauce.
Steel pans were invented in Trinidad, where musicians began making them from old oil drums.
A badminton shuttlecock can fly faster than 400 kilometres an hour, which makes it the fastest ball in any racket sport.
Pumice is a volcanic rock so full of air bubbles that it can float on water.
Jellyfish have been around for hundreds of millions of years, and they have no brain, no heart and no bones.
A pineapple plant takes about two years to grow a single pineapple.
A flea can jump more than 100 times its own length.
The equals sign was invented in 1557 by Robert Recorde, who chose two parallel lines because "no two things can be more equal".
The Eiffel Tower was built for a fair in 1889 and was only meant to stand for 20 years.
The Louvre in Paris is the most visited museum in the world.
There are 118 different elements on the periodic table.
A decade is ten years, a century is 100, and a millennium is 1,000.
Jane Goodall began studying chimpanzees in the wild in Tanzania in 1960 and discovered that they make and use tools.
Magpies are among the few animals that recognise themselves in a mirror.
Crocodiles' relatives were already around in the time of the dinosaurs, and some of them were as big as buses.
Beavers have orange teeth, because they contain iron, which makes them extra strong.
Children have 20 baby teeth, and grown-ups have 32 adult teeth.
A tiger's stripes are on its skin too, not just its fur.
A group of pugs is called a grumble.
Honeybees tell each other where flowers are by dancing. The angle of the dance shows the direction.
Tetris was made in 1984 in the Soviet Union by Alexey Pajitnov. He named it after "tetra", the Greek word for four, and his love of tennis.
Joseph Grimaldi, born in 1778, became such a famous clown that clowns are still nicknamed "Joey" after him.
Comet tails always point away from the Sun, even when the comet is heading away from it.
Nearly all the internet between countries travels through cables lying on the sea floor.
The printing press was invented in Europe around 1440 by Johannes Gutenberg, and made books cheap enough for ordinary people.
Woolly mammoths were still alive when the Egyptians were building the pyramids.
The first traffic light was put up outside the Houses of Parliament in London in 1868. It was worked by a person and lit by gas.
Vatican City, in Rome, is the smallest country in the world. You could walk across it in about ten minutes.
Bluetooth is named after a Viking king, Harald Bluetooth, who brought together the people of Denmark and Norway.
People can hear sounds from about 20 to 20,000 vibrations a second. Dogs can hear much higher sounds than we can.
Judo means "gentle way", and karate means "empty hand".
A moonbow is a rainbow made by moonlight instead of sunlight.
The blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived, even bigger than the biggest dinosaurs.
Trees can share food and signals through networks of fungus under the ground, which some scientists call the "wood wide web".
Dung beetles can find their way in a straight line by looking at the Milky Way.
A million seconds is about 11 and a half days. A billion seconds is about 32 years.
Petra, in Jordan, is a city carved into pink-red rock cliffs.
Kintsugi is a Japanese art where broken pots are mended with gold, so the cracks become part of the design.
Hydrogen is the most common element in the universe.
At the North and South Poles, the Sun rises and sets only once a year, so there are about six months of day and six months of night.
Tim Berners-Lee came up with the World Wide Web in 1989, and it was made free for everyone to use.
A cuckoo lays its eggs in other birds' nests, and the other birds raise the chick.
A camel's hump stores fat, not water.
Your thumb has two bones, but your other fingers have three.
Octopuses have blue blood, because they use copper, not iron, to carry oxygen around.
Many games draw 60 pictures every second. A cartoon film usually uses 24.
The Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon, and about 400 times further away. That is why the Moon can just cover it in a total eclipse.
The first computer "bug" was a real moth, found stuck inside a computer at Harvard in 1947.
The dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago, after a huge asteroid hit what is now Mexico.
LEGO gets its name from two Danish words, "leg godt", which mean "play well".
The Atlantic Ocean is slowly getting wider, by about two and a half centimetres a year, about as fast as your fingernails grow.
In Italian, the @ sign is called a "snail". In Dutch it is a "monkey's tail".
Humpback whales sing long songs that can last 10 to 20 minutes, and the whole group changes the song over time.
The five rings on the Olympic flag are said to stand for five parts of the world joined together.
The northern lights happen when tiny particles from the Sun hit the air high above the Earth and make it glow.
Sharks have skeletons made of cartilage, the same bendy material as the tip of your nose, and not bone.
A date palm seed that was about 2,000 years old, found in an ancient fortress in Israel, was planted and grew.
Some cicadas spend 13 or 17 years underground before climbing out all at once.
Roman numerals have no zero.
Maglev trains float just above the track on magnets, and a test train in Japan has gone faster than 600 kilometres an hour.
The Bayeux Tapestry, almost 70 metres long, tells the story of the Battle of Hastings in 1066 in stitches.
A grown-up's body is about 60 per cent water.
The longest day of the year is in June in the northern half of the world, and in December in the southern half.
A kiwi, which cannot fly, lays an egg that is about a fifth of the weight of its body.
Scientists think that zebra stripes may stop biting flies from landing on them.
Starfish have no brain and no blood. They pump sea water around their bodies instead.
Speedrunners can finish Super Mario Bros in under five minutes by finding clever shortcuts.
At the centre of our galaxy is a giant black hole called Sagittarius A*, with about four million times the mass of the Sun.
Aerogel is a solid that is mostly air. It is so light that it is sometimes called "frozen smoke".
Megalodon was a giant shark that died out about three and a half million years ago. Its teeth were as big as a person's hand.
The first item ever scanned with a barcode, in 1974, was a packet of chewing gum.
Istanbul, in Turkey, is built on two continents: Europe and Asia.
British Sign Language and American Sign Language are different languages, with their own words and grammar.
A grand piano has more than 200 strings inside it.
A sailing boat can sail towards the wind by zig-zagging, which is called tacking.
Parts of the Atacama Desert in Chile have gone for years with no rain at all.
Shark skin is covered in tiny tooth-like scales, which is why it feels rough if you stroke it the wrong way.
Rafflesia is the biggest single flower in the world, up to about a metre across, and it smells like rotting meat.
Only female mosquitoes bite.
Honeycomb cells are hexagons, which fit together with no gaps and use the least wax.
Concorde could fly across the Atlantic Ocean in a little over three hours.
Hans Christian Andersen, who wrote The Little Mermaid, was born in Denmark in 1805.
Liquid nitrogen is so cold, about minus 196 degrees Celsius, that it freezes flowers so hard they shatter.
In many tropical countries, the year is divided into wet and dry seasons instead of summer and winter.
Barn owls can hear a mouse moving, even under leaves or snow.
A cat spends about two thirds of its life asleep.
A mantis shrimp punches so fast that the water around its claw forms bubbles that burst with a shockwave.
The creator of Zelda, Shigeru Miyamoto, said the series was inspired by exploring woods and caves as a boy.
Neptune has the fastest winds of any planet we know, over 2,000 kilometres an hour.
Velcro was invented after a Swiss engineer noticed burrs stuck to his dog's fur.
Pterosaurs such as Pteranodon were not dinosaurs. They were flying reptiles.
Super Glue was discovered by accident, when scientists were trying to make clear plastic for gun sights.
The Great Barrier Reef, off Australia, is the biggest living structure on Earth. It is built by billions of tiny animals called coral polyps.
Esperanto is a language invented in 1887, designed so that people all over the world could learn it easily.
The harp is the national symbol of Ireland.
The butterfly stroke in swimming was developed in the 1930s as a variation on breaststroke.
Lightning strikes somewhere on Earth about 100 times every second.
